Leopardess Consulting · brand · L2

Six leopardess logo marks

All six are the agreed concept — a stylised leopardess head in profile, antique gold on charcoal, generated by the same model the chassis uses (Gemini "Banana"). The deciding test is the row at the bottom of each card: a logo has to survive at 16 and 32 pixels, because that is a browser tab. The solid-fill marks hold; the fine line-art ones do not. My recommendation is the first card.

Solid mark, spots as negative space

Recommended

A filled gold silhouette with the rosettes knocked out as holes. This is the one that behaves like a logo: it survives to 16px, it will reverse cleanly (gold on dark, or dark on gold), and there is exactly one of it — no stray strokes to break. Unmistakably a leopardess. My pick for the permanent mark.

At favicon size c2_solid_negative

Head emerging from the spot pattern

Strong

The head is built from the rosettes themselves, densest at the skull and thinning toward the neck. More characterful and more obviously *leopard* than any other option, and the spot motif here is the thing we can lift out and repeat across the site as a texture. Slightly busier at tiny sizes than c2, but still reads.

At favicon size c3_spots_forming

Faceted, geometric

Strong

Built from flat planes with diamond spots. The most modern and the most "tech" of the set — it would sit well next to talk of infrastructure. Holds up small because the shapes are large. Risk: faceted animal heads are a common studio move, so it is the least distinctive idea even though the execution is clean.

At favicon size c6_geometric

Minimal continuous line

Backup

The most elegant and the quietest — a few confident strokes. Beautiful at large sizes and on a business card, but the thin line is exactly what dissolves at favicon size (see the 32px row). Usable if we pair it with a solid-fill favicon variant, which is more moving parts.

At favicon size c4_minimal_strokes

Single-line, detailed

Consider

A continuous-line treatment with more anatomical detail than c4. Handsome on screen, same small-size weakness as c4, and the extra internal lines make it worse at 16px, not better.

At favicon size c1_continuous_line

Enclosed badge

Consider

The head inside a ring, as a badge. The ring reads at any size, which is a real advantage for a favicon, but the head inside turns to mush small, so at 16px you get "a gold ring with something in it" rather than a cat. Better as a large seal than a working logo.

At favicon size c5_circle_badge

How the chosen mark becomes the real logo (no special tools)

These previews were generated directly against the Gemini image API for speed of review. The permanent logo will be produced through the chassis' own pipeline so it is reproducible without anything outside the platform:

  1. Deploy the one-line routing change already committed to dynamic_adapter.go (routes logo to Banana so the mark can carry a reference image).
  2. Insert a site_plan_imagery row, kind=logo, asset_key=logo, with the winning prompt (RUNBOOK O5).
  3. Let image-build-handler generate and asset-deployer commit it to /assets/images/logo.png; set sites.logo_url to match.
  4. Derive the favicon and social card from the same file, and generate every later site image with this logo as the reference so the whole set stays one family.

The exact prompts for all six are saved beside this page in PROMPTS.md, so the pipeline can reproduce the chosen direction verbatim.
